description: Build the hardened bare-EC2 launch path that removes every single-point-of-failure from the prior run, and prove it works without launching anything. The prior run died because the benchmark lived inside an interactive session: no user-data, no IAM instance profile (so no SSM shell), a key pair whose private key vanished with the session, nothing streamed off the box, no self-termination, and the 142-160 GB checkpoint written to a 200 GB root volume instead of the 30.4 TB of local NVMe. This feature produces scripts/bootstrap/bench-bootstrap.sh (the user-data payload, fully self-driving) and scripts/launch-bench-ec2.sh (the launcher), plus tests/ which runs the bootstrap under stubbed aws/docker/nvidia-smi/mdadm/curl binaries so the control flow is actually executed and asserted on a GPU-less sandbox. Nothing is launched: validation is `run-instances --dry-run` plus the stub harness. Depends on FEAT-001 for the bucket name, instance profile name and preflight helpers.
steps: Create scripts/bootstrap/bench-bootstrap.sh, the script that will be passed as EC2 user-data. Same house style as scripts/run-benchmark.sh (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, banner, all-caps `VAR="${VAR:-default}"` config block, `log()` helper with the `[%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S]` prefix, `# ===` section separators with `Step a)`-style labels). Every tunable must come from an environment prelude that launch-bench-ec2.sh renders above the script body, so the same file is testable locally with those variables set by hand. Add a DRY_RUN guard so that when DRY_RUN=1 the script logs the commands it would run for the genuinely destructive operations (mdadm create, mkfs, shutdown/terminate) instead of executing them, while still executing all of the surrounding control flow.

bootstrap Step a) - fail-loud logging: redirect all stdout/stderr to /var/log/tpot-bench/bootstrap.log via `exec > >(tee -a ...) 2>&1` and install an ERR trap plus an EXIT trap that records the exit status and a one-line reason into a status file (e.g. /var/log/tpot-bench/status.json with fields phase, exit_code, message, timestamp). Every phase transition must update that file so an outside observer can tell exactly where a run stopped. This is the fix for the prior run's total lack of observability.

bootstrap Step b) - NVMe: enumerate local instance-store devices robustly rather than guessing paths. Use `lsblk -dn -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL` / `nvme list` and select devices whose model identifies them as Amazon EC2 NVMe Instance Storage, explicitly excluding the EBS root device. If more than one is found, assemble RAID0 with `mdadm --create /dev/md0 --level=0 --raid-devices=N ...`; if exactly one is found use it directly (this is what makes the same code path testable on c5d.large and g6e.xlarge, which have a single 50 GB / 250 GB disk). mkfs.xfs (or ext4 if xfs tooling is absent) and mount at /mnt/nvme. Then assert free space with `df --output=avail` and FAIL FAST with a clear message if free space is less than the checkpoint size plus a configurable margin, before downloading a single byte. Point HF_HOME, HF_HUB_CACHE, TMPDIR and the Docker data-root at /mnt/nvme (moving Docker's data-root requires stopping dockerd, relocating /var/lib/docker and restarting it - do that before pulling the image so the ~13 GB image also lands on NVMe, not the root volume). README section 9.1 documents that HyperPod uses /opt/dlami/nvme/ and self-built EKS RAID0 uses /mnt/k8s-disks/0/; this bare-EC2 path standardises on /mnt/nvme and must not hardcode either of the other two.

bootstrap Step c) - continuous off-box persistence: start a background streamer loop that every STREAM_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 30) runs `aws s3 sync /var/log/tpot-bench/ s3://$RESULTS_BUCKET/runs/$RUN_ID/logs/` and `aws s3 sync /mnt/nvme/results/ s3://$RESULTS_BUCKET/runs/$RUN_ID/results/`, and also publishes a CloudWatch heartbeat metric (namespace TpotBench, metric Heartbeat, dimension RunId, plus a Phase-encoded metric) via `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data`. Record the streamer PID and reap it in the EXIT trap. This is what makes an unresponsive orchestrating session survivable: partial logs and partial results are already off the box.

bootstrap Step d) - GPU telemetry: the prior run had zero GPU metrics, so GPU idleness could only be inferred. Add a sampler loop that runs `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used,memory.total,temperature.gpu --format=csv,noheader,nounits` on an interval, appends to /var/log/tpot-bench/gpu.csv (which the streamer therefore ships to S3), and publishes at least GPU utilization and memory used to the TpotBench CloudWatch namespace. Skip the loop gracefully with a logged warning when nvidia-smi is absent, so the non-GPU c5d.large plumbing stage still works.

bootstrap Step e) - model fetch: download the checkpoint into /mnt/nvme/hf-cache. Prefer an in-region S3 mirror when CHECKPOINT_S3_URI is set (`aws s3 sync`), otherwise fall back to `hf download` / huggingface_hub with resume enabled. Log the total bytes fetched and elapsed time. After the fetch, re-assert free space. The prior run downloaded ~151 GB twice for a total of 315 GB NetworkIn; the resume-capable fetch plus the FEAT-003 S3 mirror is what prevents a repeat.

bootstrap Step f) - serve and bench: `docker run` the SGLang image with `--gpus all`, `--ipc=host` or an explicit `--shm-size`, `--ulimit memlock=-1`, and /mnt/nvme mounted so HF_HOME resolves inside the container. Launch the server with parameters supplied entirely from the rendered env prelude (model path, tp, speculative flags, mem-fraction-static, host 0.0.0.0, port 30000) so no recipe is baked into the bootstrap. Poll http://localhost:30000/health until ready with a timeout of at least SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT (default 2400s, because the cookbook warns the first cold start takes 10-15 minutes for FlashInfer autotune and CUDA graph capture, and run-benchmark.sh already uses POD_READY_TIMEOUT=2400). Then run the two bench_serving commands from README section 6.1 with their exact parameters unchanged: `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --num-prompts 50 --max-concurrency 1` with `--random-input 40000 --random-output 1500`, then again with `--random-input 30000 --random-output 4096`. Capture the server's stdout/stderr to /var/log/tpot-bench/sglang-server.log unconditionally, including on failure, since that log is the only way to diagnose a startup crash after the box is gone.

bootstrap Step g) - spot interruption handling: poll http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/instance-action using IMDSv2 (PUT to /latest/api/token first, then pass X-aws-ec2-metadata-token) on a short interval; on notice, log it, force an immediate final s3 sync, mark status.json with phase=spot_interrupted, and exit cleanly. README section 12.13 sketches this pattern; implement it properly with IMDSv2 rather than the unauthenticated form.

bootstrap Step h) - watchdog and self-termination: two independent triggers must terminate the instance. (1) Normal completion: after the final s3 sync succeeds, self-terminate. (2) Hard wall-clock deadline: a background timer that fires after MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES (default 240) regardless of what the main flow is doing, syncs whatever exists, and terminates. Self-terminate via `aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids <own id from IMDSv2>` with `shutdown -h now` as a fallback if the API call fails; the instance profile from FEAT-001 grants TerminateInstances conditioned on the Project=tpot-benchmark tag, so the launcher MUST apply that tag or self-termination will be denied. A 13h14m runaway at $26.67/hr cost ~$353 last time; a 240-minute ceiling caps the worst case near $107 and the deadline must hold even if the main script hangs.

Create scripts/launch-bench-ec2.sh, the launcher, in the same house style. It renders the env prelude + bench-bootstrap.sh into a single user-data document, validates the rendered document with `bash -n` before ever sending it, base64-encodes it if required, and calls `aws ec2 run-instances` with: --instance-market-options spot one-time with a MaxPrice ceiling, --iam-instance-profile Name=tpot-bench-ec2-profile, --image-id from the FEAT-001 dynamic AMI resolution, --subnet-id, --security-group-ids, --instance-type, a root --block-device-mappings sized modestly (the checkpoint no longer lives there, but leave room for the OS; do not rely on the root volume for model weights), --metadata-options requiring IMDSv2 (HttpTokens=required), and --tag-specifications applying Name plus Project=tpot-benchmark plus RunId. Also apply the tags to the volumes. Generate RUN_ID as a timestamp plus short random suffix and print it prominently, since every S3 path and CloudWatch dimension keys off it.

launcher: create or reuse a security group that has NO inbound rules at all (SSM works purely outbound over HTTPS, so no SSH ingress is needed) and egress open. Do not reuse the 0.0.0.0/0 SSH posture of sg-0775ac013a1b6080d. If an --allow-ssh-from flag is passed, restrict the rule to the caller's egress IP resolved at run time from https://checkip.amazonaws.com, never 0.0.0.0/0, and never hardcode 54.236.10.181.

launcher: enforce the spend gate. Without CONFIRM_SPEND=yes in the environment the launcher must print the exact instance type, AZ, spot ceiling, estimated hourly cost, MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES and the resulting worst-case dollar figure, then refuse to launch and exit non-zero. With --dry-run it must pass --dry-run through to run-instances and treat DryRunOperation as success. Default behaviour with no flags must be the refusal, not a launch.

launcher: add --wait mode that, after a real launch, polls the CloudWatch heartbeat metric and `aws s3 ls` of the run prefix and tails the streamed bootstrap.log from S3, so an operator gets live progress without SSH and without a live session holding state. Also print the ready-to-paste `aws ssm start-session --target <id> --region us-east-2` command.

Create tests/run-tests.sh plus tests/stubs/ containing fake `aws`, `docker`, `nvidia-smi`, `lsblk`, `nvme`, `mdadm`, `mkfs.xfs`, `mount`, `df`, `curl`, `shutdown` executables that log their invocations to a temp file and return scripted output. Prepend tests/stubs to PATH and run bench-bootstrap.sh with DRY_RUN=1 for each case. The tests must assert on real behaviour, not on static strings: (1) single-instance-store disk is used directly and mdadm is NOT invoked; (2) multiple disks trigger `mdadm --create` with --level=0 and the correct --raid-devices count, and the EBS root device is never included; (3) when the stubbed `df` reports less free space than the checkpoint size, the script exits non-zero BEFORE any download or docker command is invoked (assert the stub invocation log contains no s3 sync and no docker run); (4) the streamer performs an `s3 sync` of both the log dir and the results dir to the expected s3://bucket/runs/RUN_ID/... prefixes; (5) the spot-interruption path, when the stubbed metadata endpoint returns an action, triggers a final sync and sets status.json phase=spot_interrupted; (6) the wall-clock deadline path fires with a very small MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES and results in a terminate-instances call in the stub log; (7) normal completion results in exactly one terminate-instances call; (8) nvidia-smi missing produces a warning and does not abort; (9) launch-bench-ec2.sh without CONFIRM_SPEND exits non-zero and its stub log contains no run-instances call lacking --dry-run. Each case must fail if the corresponding logic is removed - verify that by temporarily breaking the code and confirming the test goes red, and note in findings which cases you confirmed this way.

Run `bash scripts/launch-bench-ec2.sh --stage full --dry-run` against real AWS (dry-run only) and confirm the DryRunOperation response, then paste the rendered user-data size (user-data has a 16 KB limit after base64 encoding - if the rendered document approaches that, have the launcher upload the bootstrap to S3 and reduce user-data to a small fetch-and-exec stub, and state which approach you used in findings).
acceptance_criteria: `bash tests/run-tests.sh` passes all 9 cases listed in the steps and exits 0.
The disk-space guard case proves the script aborts before any download: the stub invocation log for that case contains zero `s3 sync` and zero `docker run` entries.

The multi-disk case proves RAID0 assembly: the stub log contains an `mdadm --create` invocation with `--level=0` and a --raid-devices count matching the number of stubbed instance-store disks, and the EBS root device name does not appear in that invocation.
The deadline case proves the watchdog is independent of the main flow: with MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES set to a fraction of a minute, the stub log contains a `terminate-instances` invocation.
`bash scripts/launch-bench-ec2.sh --stage full --dry-run` returns the AWS DryRunOperation result and exits 0 without creating an instance.
`bash scripts/launch-bench-ec2.sh --stage full` with CONFIRM_SPEND unset exits non-zero, prints the instance type, spot ceiling, estimated $/hr and worst-case total, and makes no run-instances call.

The rendered user-data document passes `bash -n` inside the launcher before any AWS call is made; demonstrate by injecting a deliberate syntax error into the bootstrap and confirming the launcher refuses.
grep confirms the run-instances invocation includes `--iam-instance-profile`, `HttpTokens=required`, `Project=tpot-benchmark` and a spot MaxPrice, since self-termination and SSM both depend on them.
No literal 0.0.0.0/0 appears in any new script, and the literal 54.236.10.181 appears nowhere.
`aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-2 --filters Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running` still returns empty after this feature: nothing was launched and nothing was billed.
verification: env -u CONFIRM_SPEND bash scripts/launch-bench-ec2.sh --stage full ; test $? -ne 0
aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-2 --filters Name=instance-state-name,Values=pending,running --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId' --output text  (expect empty)
findings:

Zero compute spend, zero AWS mutations: nothing was launched, no spot request created, the S3 bucket is still empty (verified with `aws s3 ls --recursive` = no objects), and `describe-instances --filters state=pending,running` still returns empty. The only AWS calls made were sts/ssm/describe-*/s3 ls plus run-instances --dry-run.

=== USER-DATA SIZE: THE S3-HOSTED FALLBACK IS REQUIRED (not optional) ===
Rendered inline document for --stage full = 41827 bytes raw / 55772 bytes base64. EC2's raw user-data limit is 16384 bytes, so the inline form is 2.55x over and the launcher automatically switches to the S3-hosted mode described in the step: it uploads bench-bootstrap.sh to s3://<bucket>/bootstrap/<RUN_ID>/bench-bootstrap.sh and reduces user-data to a 2821-byte (base64 3764) stub = env prelude + `aws s3 cp` retry loop (30 attempts x 10s, because the instance profile can take a moment to become usable) + `exec`. If the stub cannot retrieve the script after 30 attempts it terminates the instance instead of idling at $26.67/hr - that failure mode would otherwise be a silent money burn. In --dry-run the upload is skipped and logged; both the inline and the stub documents are `bash -n` validated. Sizes per stage: plumbing 42065/2823, gpu-smoke 42057/2815, full 41827/2821. An alternative would have been gzip (cloud-init accepts gzipped user-data, ~8 KB compressed) but the plan mandated the S3 approach and S3 also gives the operator an auditable copy of exactly what ran.

=== FAIL-ON-BREAK VERIFIED FOR ALL 12 CASES (13 break scenarios) ===
Method: copy scripts/ + tests/ into a temp dir, apply one surgical patch there, run the suite, confirm the target case flips to FAIL, discard the copy. The repo files were never left broken. Results (all '按预期变红'):
  case 1  <- `elif [[ ${#NVME_DEVICES[@]} -eq 1 ]]` forced false, so a single disk also goes through RAID0 -> mdadm appears -> red.
  case 2  <- `--raid-devices="${#NVME_DEVICES[@]}"` hardcoded to 2 -> red.
  case 3  <- the `assert_free_space "下载前"` call removed from the main flow -> s3 sync + docker run appear -> red.
  case 4  <- `start_streamer` removed -> periodic sync count drops from 9 to 2 and the '[streamer] 第 N 次' traces vanish -> red.
  case 5  <- `start_spot_watcher` removed -> phase ends 'completed' instead of 'spot_interrupted' -> red.
  case 6  <- `start_watchdog` removed -> no deadline_exceeded phase -> red.
  case 6  <- the exactly-once noclobber guard in terminate_self() removed -> two terminate-instances calls -> red.
  case 7  <- `--num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS"` changed to `--num-prompts 10` (deviating from README 6.1) -> red.
  case 8  <- the `command -v nvidia-smi` guard removed -> warning gone, gpu.csv created on a GPU-less box -> red.
  case 9  <- the `CONFIRM_SPEND != yes` branch forced false -> launcher proceeds -> red.
  case 10 <- `--iam-instance-profile` dropped from the run-instances arg list -> red.
  case 11 <- both `bash -n` guards in the launcher forced false -> a syntactically broken bootstrap reaches AWS -> red.
  case 12 <- a world-CIDR literal injected into the launcher -> red.
The two driver scripts lived in .scratch/ (gitignored) and were deleted afterwards.

=== TWO REAL BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT (both fixed) ===
1. status.json write race. write_status() used a single `$STATUS_FILE.tmp` for every writer. The main shell and the Spot watcher wrote concurrently, one `mv` lost its temp file, `mv` failed, the ERR trap fired and the whole run died with exit 143 in a scenario that should have exited 0. Fix: the temp path now includes $BASHPID (differs per subshell) and the `mv` is `|| true` so a status write can never kill a run.
2. Terminal-phase downgrade. Background workers cannot mutate the main shell's $PHASE, so after the watcher set phase=spot_interrupted the main flow's next set_phase overwrote it and an outside observer saw '卡在 fetching_model' instead of 'Spot 回收'. Fix: workers call mark_terminal_phase() which writes $LOG_DIR/.terminal-phase; write_status() adopts that value and refuses to downgrade, and on_exit reads it to pick the final phase and message.

=== DESIGN DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING ===
- DRY_RUN semantics: run_destructive() logs the full command line to $DRY_RUN_LOG instead of executing when DRY_RUN=1. It covers `mdadm --create`, `mkfs.xfs`/`mkfs.ext4`, `mount`, the docker data-root relocation, `aws ec2 terminate-instances` and `shutdown -h now`. tests/run-tests.sh sets DRY_RUN_LOG=$STUB_LOG so stub invocations and dry-run-recorded commands land in ONE invocation log; assertions therefore read the command line the real logic computed (device list, disk count, own instance-id), not a static string. This is what lets 'the stub log contains mdadm --create with --level=0 and --raid-devices=4' be both true and safe on a machine with no NVMe.
- The disk-guard criterion ('zero s3 sync, zero docker run') conflicts with wanting logs off-box on failure, because the streamer starts after the guard. Resolved by persist_final(): if the streamer never started it uploads bootstrap.log and status.json with a single `aws s3 cp` each. So a guard failure is still visible from S3 while the invocation log contains zero `s3 sync` entries. Case 3 asserts both.
- The EXIT trap always self-terminates (exactly once, enforced by an O_EXCL flag file), including on failure. SELF_TERMINATE=false disables it for debugging. Default is terminate, because 'keep it alive so I can look at it later' is precisely how 13h14m got billed.
- Startup order in the main flow is deliberate: init_logging -> start_watchdog (before anything that can hang) -> setup_storage -> assert_free_space (before any download) -> start_streamer -> start_gpu_sampler -> start_spot_watcher -> relocate_docker_data_root (before docker pull, so the ~13 GB image lands on NVMe) -> fetch_checkpoint -> serve_and_bench -> finalize.
- Every background worker begins with `trap - EXIT ERR TERM INT`; without it a `( ... ) &` subshell inherits the EXIT trap and runs the whole cleanup path (including self-termination) when it exits.
- MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES accepts fractions (the deadline is `awk printf %.0f` of minutes*60, floored to 1s), which is how case 6 exercises the watchdog in 3 seconds.

=== AWS / TOOLING BEHAVIOUR RESOLVED DURING THIS FEATURE ===
- InvalidBlockDeviceMapping: 'Volume of size 30GB is smaller than snapshot snap-08de08bab69bb43e4, expect size >= 75GB'. The Deep Learning Base OSS Nvidia Driver GPU AMI root snapshot is 75 GB, so ROOT_VOLUME_GB can never be below that. The plumbing stage's original 30 GB was rejected by dry-run and is now 80 GB (gp3, 20 minutes = fractions of a cent). gpu-smoke 100 GB, full 200 GB.
- `describe-spot-price-history` accepts `--availability-zone` to get a single AZ's price directly, which avoids the per-AZ parsing preflight.sh does. `--start-time` still needs the ISO-8601 form `$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')` as FEAT-001 recorded.
- The spend refusal exits 2 (not 1) so a caller can distinguish 'refused, nothing happened' from a genuine error.
- No SG was created: SECURITY_GROUP_ID defaults to sg-0775ac013a1b6080d, whose ingress FEAT-001 emptied, and the launcher re-verifies at launch time that no world-CIDR ingress rule exists, refusing to launch if one reappears. `--create-sg` (creates a group with no inbound rules at all) and `--allow-ssh-from CIDR|auto` (resolves the caller's egress IP from https://checkip.amazonaws.com at run time and only ever authorises a single /32) exist but were not exercised, because both mutate AWS. The world-CIDR string is never written as a literal anywhere; it is built with `printf '%s/%d' '0.0.0.0' 0` for comparisons, and case 12 greps all three new scripts for both that literal and 54.236.10.181.
- shellcheck via `docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/mnt" -w /mnt koalaman/shellcheck:stable ...` also checks the extension-less stub files correctly (it reads the shebang).

=== SGLANG NOTES (bootstrap bakes NO recipe) ===
The bootstrap assembles `--model-path --tp --mem-fraction-static --trust-remote-code --host --port` from prelude variables and appends $SGLANG_EXTRA_ARGS verbatim; $SGLANG_SERVE_ARGS, if non-empty, replaces the whole assembled string. So the EAGLE / DSPARK / DP-attention decisions live entirely in FEAT-003's recipe files. The correct flag is `--speculative-algorithm` (run-benchmark.sh's `--speculative-algo` is still wrong; fixing it is FEAT-003's job, untouched here). Case 7 proves pass-through by asserting `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE` reaches the docker run command line. Server launch uses `--gpus all --ipc=host --shm-size 64g --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 --network host -v /mnt/nvme:/mnt/nvme` with HF_HOME/HF_HUB_CACHE/TMPDIR pointed at NVMe, `docker logs -f` teed to /var/log/tpot-bench/sglang-server.log unconditionally, and readiness polled on /health for SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT=2400s (the cookbook's 10-15 min cold start for FlashInfer autotune plus graph capture).

=== CONTRACTS FEAT-003 MUST CONSUME ===
1. Recipe files: pass `--recipe FILE`; the file's contents are appended verbatim to the rendered env prelude (after the standard exports, so it can override any of them). It must be valid bash - `export VAR=value` lines. Useful knobs: MODEL_NAME, CHECKPOINT_GB, TP_SIZE, MEM_FRACTION_STATIC, SGLANG_IMAGE, SGLANG_LAUNCH_CMD, SGLANG_EXTRA_ARGS, SGLANG_SERVE_ARGS, INPUT_TOKENS/OUTPUT_TOKENS/OFFICIAL_INPUT_TOKENS/OFFICIAL_OUTPUT_TOKENS/NUM_PROMPTS/MAX_CONCURRENCY, SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT, SHM_SIZE, STORAGE_MARGIN_GB, MAX_RUNTIME_MINUTES.
2. Launcher CLI for the staged runner: `scripts/launch-bench-ec2.sh --stage {plumbing|gpu-smoke|full} [--recipe F] [--checkpoint-s3-uri URI] [--dry-run] [--wait]`. Stage defaults - plumbing: c5d.large, max-price 0.20, 20 min, FETCH_CHECKPOINT=false, RUN_SERVER=false, root 80 GB; gpu-smoke: g6e.xlarge, max-price 2.00, 60 min, model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (a deliberate placeholder - override it in a recipe if you want something else), tp 1, 2000/256 tokens x 4 prompts, root 100 GB; full: p5en.48xlarge, max-price 35.00, 240 min, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash, tp 8, README 6.1 loads unchanged, root 200 GB. Exit codes: 0 = launched or dry-run OK, 2 = refused for want of CONFIRM_SPEND, 1 = error.
3. S3 layout written by the streamer (every STREAM_INTERVAL_SECONDS=30):
   s3://tpot-bench-results-077090643075-us-east-2/runs/<RUN_ID>/logs/     <- bootstrap.log, status.json, gpu.csv, sglang-server.log, bench-custom.log, bench-official.log, dry-run-commands.log
   s3://.../runs/<RUN_ID>/results/                                        <- bench_custom_<RUN_ID>.json, bench_official_<RUN_ID>.json, run_<RUN_ID>.json
   s3://.../bootstrap/<RUN_ID>/bench-bootstrap.sh                         <- the exact script that ran (S3-hosted mode)
   RUN_ID format: <UTC yyyymmdd-HHMMSS>-<4 hex chars>.
4. run_<RUN_ID>.json (written by write_run_metadata) is NOT the compare-results.sh schema - it is the raw inputs for FEAT-003's collector: run_id, stage, region, instance_id, instance_type, model, sglang_image, tp_size, serve_args, custom_benchmark_file, official_benchmark_file, custom_pass, official_pass, config{input_tokens,output_tokens,official_input_tokens,official_output_tokens,num_prompts,max_concurrency}, elapsed_seconds. The collector still has to emit metadata.{instance_type,tp_size,region,timestamp} and custom_benchmark/official_benchmark .config/.results/.pass to keep compare-results.sh working.
5. status.json phases, in order, for anything that polls progress: starting, storage, storage_guard, streaming, telemetry, fetching_model, starting_server, server_ready, benchmarking, finalizing, completed; terminal error phases: failed, spot_interrupted, deadline_exceeded. CloudWatch namespace TpotBench: Heartbeat (dims RunId,Stage), PhaseCode (dims RunId,Phase), GpuUtilization and GpuMemoryUsedMiB (dims RunId,GpuIndex).
6. Checkpoint mirror contract: set CHECKPOINT_S3_URI and the bootstrap runs `aws s3 sync "$CHECKPOINT_S3_URI" /mnt/nvme/models/<MODEL_NAME with / replaced by __>` instead of hitting HuggingFace; that same directory is what --model-path points at. So FEAT-003's mirror should be laid out as s3://<bucket>/checkpoints/<model-slug>/ containing the repo files at the top level. Without the variable the bootstrap falls back to `hf download` -> `huggingface-cli download --resume-download` -> `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(resume_download=True)`, all resumable.
7. Storage-reserve reconciliation: preflight.sh plans capacity as RAID0 total minus STORAGE_RESERVE_PCT=10% (27360 GB usable of 30400 GB on p5en.48xlarge). The bootstrap instead asserts an absolute floor - free space on /mnt/nvme must be >= CHECKPOINT_GB + STORAGE_MARGIN_GB (160 + 80 = 240 GB for the full stage) both before and after the fetch. The two agree for every planned configuration (240 << 27360); if a future recipe changes CHECKPOINT_GB, pass a matching STORAGE_MARGIN_GB rather than editing the percentage.
8. run-instances stays parameter-compatible with the list preflight.sh dry-runs, plus: `--user-data file://<rendered>`, RunId and Stage tags, and a second `--tag-specifications ResourceType=volume,...` so volumes carry Project/Name/RunId/Stage too. Project=tpot-benchmark is mandatory - the IAM condition on ec2:TerminateInstances means self-termination is denied without it.

- 12 test cases instead of 9. Cases 1-9 are exactly the ones listed in the steps; 10 (dry-run run-instances argument completeness: --iam-instance-profile, HttpTokens=required, Project=tpot-benchmark, MaxPrice, SpotInstanceType=one-time, ResourceType=volume, --user-data file://, --instance-type), 11 (a deliberately broken bootstrap must be refused before any AWS call, which is the acceptance criterion about injecting a syntax error) and 12 (grep for the world-CIDR literal and 54.236.10.181) were added because three acceptance criteria are otherwise only checked by hand.

Its AWS calls are all read-only.
